## About Me

I am a PhD candidate in Economics at the **University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa**, where I study environmental, urban, and spatial economics.

My research focuses on how environmental risks and natural disasters affect housing markets, households, and local economic outcomes. I use spatial, administrative, environmental, economic, weather, and nighttime-lights data to examine these questions.

I am currently on the **2026–27 academic job market**.

Before and alongside my academic research, I have worked on economic policy and applied research. I served as a Short-Term Consultant with the **World Bank's Macroeconomics, Trade & Investment Global Practice** in the Nepal Country Office, where I contributed to analytical work on macroeconomics, public finance, and subnational fiscal policy.

I also work as a Graduate Research Assistant at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa on research examining the health, social, and economic impacts of the 2023 Maui wildfires.
